query: Our approach has multiple advantages over existing methyltransferase-based sequencing approaches: first, by using a relatively nonspecific methyltransferase, we avoid the primary sequence biases associated with GpC/CpG methyltransferase footprinting methods; second, by natively detecting modifications using the single-molecule real-time sequencer, we reduce enzymatic sequence bias and avoid sample damage associated with sodium bisulphite conversion; finally, and most importantly, our approach unlocks the study of protein-DNA interactions at length-scales previously unallowed by Illumina sequencing.
